nodes.content: Develop a learned surrogate for compressible Euler dynamics that preserves conservation and entropy admissibility across shocks on unseen meshes.
requirements: Keep normalized mass, momentum, and energy drift below 10⁻⁶ over 1,000 periodic, unforced timesteps.
Match an entropy-stable finite-volume baseline’s shock accuracy without increasing discrete entropy violations on unseen meshes.

nodes.content: Learn mesh-equivariant shared-face flux corrections to an entropy-stable finite-volume baseline; project fluxes onto facewise entropy constraints and positivity limits.
Does facewise entropy projection increase shock-location error on unseen triangular meshes relative to the entropy-stable baseline?
On unseen triangular meshes, facewise projection increases mean shock-location error by no more than 0.25 cells versus the baseline.
Run TriShock-2D on 40 unseen triangular meshes, comparing projected surrogate and baseline mean shock-location errors in cell widths.
On TriShock-2D’s 40 unseen meshes, projected mean shock-location error was 1.04 cells versus baseline’s 0.62: a 0.42-cell increase.
Entropy-admissible shock-sensor blending of projected and baseline fluxes reduces TriShock-2D shock-error increase from 0.42 to ≤0.25 cells.
Implement pressure-jump-triggered, entropy-constrained flux blending; rerun TriShock-2D’s 40 unseen meshes, comparing shock-location error and entropy violations against baseline.
On TriShock-2D’s 40 unseen meshes, blending yielded 0.80-cell shock error versus baseline’s 0.62, with zero excess entropy violations.
Adopt entropy-constrained shock-sensor blending: its 0.18-cell shock-error increase meets the 0.25-cell tolerance without excess entropy violations.
With adopted blending, audit 1,000-step periodic mass/momentum/energy drift below 10⁻⁶ and recheck unseen-mesh shock error and entropy violations.
Audit normalized mass, momentum, and energy drift over 1,000 periodic steps; compare TriShock-2D shock error and entropy violations against baseline.
EulerAudit-v1 report containing 1,000-step normalized drift traces and TriShock-2D shock-error and entropy-violation comparisons against the finite-volume baseline.
Review EulerAudit-v1 against acceptance gates: each normalized drift <10⁻⁶, shock-error increase ≤0.25 cells, and zero excess entropy violations.
EulerAudit-v1: normalized mass/momentum/energy drifts were 2.1/3.4/4.7×10⁻⁸ over 1,000 periodic steps; shock error 0.80 versus 0.62 cells; zero excess entropy violations.
Run MeshShift-2D on unseen skewed meshes, ablating shared-face flux correction and entropy projection; compare 1,000-step drift, shock error, entropy violations.
MeshShift-2D’s 30 skewed meshes showed 1.28-cell blended shock error versus baseline’s 0.70, with zero excess entropy violations.
Retain blending for TriShock-like meshes, but defer broader deployment until skewed-mesh shock-error increase falls below 0.25 cells.
Train a mesh-metric-conditioned viscosity predictor for shared-face entropy-stable fluxes, with baseline fallback when positivity or entropy constraints fail.
Can mesh-metric-conditioned viscosity reduce MeshShift-2D’s 0.58-cell shock-error gap below 0.25 cells without excess entropy violations?
Metric-conditioned viscosity lowers MeshShift-2D shock-error gap to ≤0.25 cells while preserving zero excess discrete entropy violations.
Train metric-conditioned viscosity on 200 mixed-quality meshes; evaluate MeshShift-2D’s 30 held-out skewed meshes for shock-error gap and entropy violations.
On MeshShift-2D’s 30 held-out meshes, metric-conditioned viscosity achieved 0.89-cell shock error versus baseline’s 0.70; zero excess entropy violations.
Audit metric-conditioned viscosity for 1,000-step periodic mass/momentum/energy drift (<10⁻⁶) and baseline-relative shock error and entropy on held-out meshes.
Run 1,000 unforced periodic steps on 30 held-out skewed meshes; log normalized conserved-quantity drift and entropy residuals each step.
MeshShiftAudit-v1 contains per-mesh 1,000-step mass, momentum, energy drift traces and entropy-residual logs for metric-conditioned viscosity.
Inspect MeshShiftAudit-v1 for peak drift and entropy violations; compare metric-conditioned viscosity’s shock error with baseline and record fallback rate.
MeshShiftAudit-v1: peak mass/momentum/energy drift 2.0/3.1/4.6×10⁻⁸; shock error 0.89 versus 0.70 cells; zero excess entropy violations; 3% fallback.
Learn mesh-equivariant WENO reconstruction weights; use shared entropy-stable fluxes and conservative baseline rollback on discrete entropy or positivity failure.
Will learned WENO weights preserve shock accuracy on held-out skewed meshes while entropy-triggered rollback remains rare?
On MeshShift-2D, learned WENO weights hold shock-error increase to ≤0.15 cells with entropy-triggered rollback on <5% of faces.
Train WENO-weight predictor on 200 mixed-quality meshes; evaluate shock error and facewise rollback frequency on MeshShift-2D’s 30 held-out meshes.
On MeshShift-2D’s 30 held-out meshes, learned WENO shock error was 0.94 versus baseline’s 0.70 cells; 11% facewise rollback.
Repeat MeshShift-2D evaluation across five training seeds, logging per-mesh shock-error gaps and entropy-triggered facewise rollback percentages.
Across five seeds, mean MeshShift-2D shock-error gap was 0.12 cells and facewise rollback 4.1%; four seeds met both thresholds.
Defer WENO deployment: four seeds passed, but one showed 0.24-cell shock-error increase and 11% rollback.
After deferral, regularize WENO weights against rollback; rerun five-seed MeshShift-2D shock/entropy tests and 1,000-step periodic conservation audits.
Retrain five WENO seeds with rollback-penalized weight regularization; measure MeshShift-2D shock-error gaps, facewise rollback, entropy violations, and 1,000-step conservation drift.
WENO-RollbackAudit-v1 records five-seed MeshShift-2D shock-error gaps, rollback rates, entropy violations, and 1,000-step mass/momentum/energy drift.
Check WENO-RollbackAudit-v1 per seed against ≤0.15-cell shock gap, <5% rollback, zero excess entropy violations, and <10⁻⁶ drift.
WENO-RollbackAudit-v1: all five seeds achieved ≤0.14-cell MeshShift-2D shock gaps, ≤4.6% rollback, zero excess entropy violations, and ≤6×10⁻⁸ drift.
Train an entropy-conservative discrete-gradient flux network with HLL shock dissipation and antisymmetric face updates on arbitrary meshes.
Can learned discrete-gradient fluxes match HLL shock accuracy on skewed meshes without adding entropy violations or conservation drift?
On MeshShift-2D, learned discrete-gradient fluxes keep shock-error increase ≤0.15 cells, zero excess entropy violations, and 1,000-step drift <10⁻⁶.
Train discrete-gradient flux network on 200 mixed-quality meshes; test MeshShift-2D shock error, entropy violations, and 1,000-step periodic drift against HLL.
On MeshShift-2D, learned fluxes yielded 1.01-cell shock error versus HLL’s 0.74; zero excess entropy violations, drift 5×10⁻⁸.
Entropy-bounded pressure-jump-adaptive HLL dissipation reduces MeshShift-2D shock-error gap to ≤0.15 cells, with zero excess entropy violations and <10⁻⁶ drift.
Implement entropy-bounded pressure-jump-adaptive HLL dissipation; rerun MeshShift-2D shock-error, entropy-violation, and 1,000-step periodic drift comparisons.
On MeshShift-2D, adaptive dissipation yielded 0.94-cell shock error versus HLL’s 0.74; zero excess entropy violations, drift 6×10⁻⁸.
Sweep pressure-jump thresholds and entropy bounds across five seeds; measure MeshShift-2D shock-error gaps, entropy violations, and 1,000-step drift.
Tuned pressure-jump threshold 0.12 yielded ≤0.14-cell MeshShift-2D shock gaps across five seeds, zero excess entropy violations, and ≤8×10⁻⁸ drift.
Mesh-skewness-conditioned pressure-jump thresholds yield ≤0.15-cell shock-error gaps versus HLL on unseen skewed meshes, zero excess entropy violations, and drift <10⁻⁶.
Sweep skewness-conditioned pressure-jump thresholds on 30 unseen MeshShift-2D meshes; compare shock-error gaps, entropy violations, and 1,000-step drift against HLL.
MeshShift-2D: skewness-conditioned shock error was 0.93 versus HLL’s 0.74 cells; zero excess entropy violations; 1,000-step drift 7×10⁻⁸.
Freeze tuned thresholds; test five seeds on held-out high-skewness MeshShift-2D meshes for HLL-relative shock error, entropy violations, and drift.
Five-seed held-out high-skewness tests: HLL-relative shock-error gaps ≤0.13 cells, zero excess entropy violations, 1,000-step drift ≤8×10⁻⁸.
Run paired five-seed MeshShift-2D evaluations of fixed versus skewness-conditioned thresholds, comparing HLL-relative shock gaps, entropy violations, and periodic drift.
Paired MeshShift-2D tests: fixed thresholds had ≤0.14-cell shock gaps; skewness-conditioned thresholds had 0.19–0.22, with zero excess entropy violations.
Adopt tuned fixed 0.12 threshold; reject skewness conditioning despite high-skewness gains because paired full-mesh shock gaps exceed 0.15 cells.
With fixed 0.12 threshold, compare unseen PolyShift-2D shock error and entropy violations against HLL; verify 1,000-step periodic drift <10⁻⁶.
Run fixed-threshold flux network and HLL on 40 unseen PolyShift-2D polygon meshes; log shock errors, entropy violations, and 1,000-step drift.
PolyShiftAudit-v1 contains per-mesh HLL-relative shock errors, discrete entropy-violation counts, and 1,000-step normalized conservation-drift traces.
Review PolyShiftAudit-v1 for HLL-relative shock-error gap ≤0.15 cells, zero excess entropy violations, and conservation drift <10⁻⁶.
PolyShiftAudit-v1: mean shock error 0.83 versus HLL’s 0.71 cells, zero excess entropy violations, peak conservation drift 7×10⁻⁸.
Advance fixed-threshold fluxes for wider validation; PolyShift passes all gates, while skewness conditioning fails full-mesh shock accuracy despite subset gains.
